paragraphs: The paper studies how to evolve a parametrized approximation to a partial differential equation over time. Dirac–Frenkel residual minimization chooses parameter changes that best match the equation at each instant. However, poorly conditioned parametrizations can admit several parameter velocities that produce the same time derivative of the represented solution, leaving the parameter evolution ambiguous.

The authors treat this ambiguity as useful freedom. Certain directions in parameter space do not change the solution’s instantaneous derivative; these are nullspace directions. Drawing on Onsager’s minimum-dissipation principle, they introduce a history variable resembling momentum and apply it only in those directions. This lets past motion influence which equivalent parameter velocity is selected without changing the residual-minimizing solution derivative.

The resulting dynamics retain instantaneous residual minimization while encouraging smoother parameter trajectories. That distinction matters because ordinary regularization can alter the optimization problem and introduce bias. Examples show greater robustness in singular and nearly singular settings, supporting the idea that redundant parameter freedom can help stabilize evolution rather than merely obstruct it.
icml-2026-a-dirac-frenkel-onsager-princi.tldr: Momentum restricted to redundant parameter directions stabilizes PDE solution dynamics while preserving instantaneous residual minimization.

paragraphs: AdaSCALE addresses the problem of recognizing inputs that differ from a model’s training distribution. Existing activation-shaping methods modify internal responses to help separate familiar inputs from unfamiliar ones. Although their scaling can vary by sample, they use a fixed percentile threshold to select activations, applying the same cutoff rule to samples with different characteristics.

The paper proposes making that threshold adaptive. Its central observation is that small input perturbations cause larger shifts in high-magnitude activations for out-of-distribution samples than for in-distribution samples. AdaSCALE uses this behavior to estimate how unfamiliar each sample is. It then scales likely familiar samples more strongly and likely unfamiliar samples more weakly, improving separation between their energy scores.

On ImageNet-1k across eight architectures, the authors report state-of-the-art detection performance. Relative to OptFS, they report improvements of 14.94% for near-distribution anomalies and 21.28% for more distant anomalies in average FPR@95. These findings support adapting activation shaping to each sample’s estimated familiarity instead of relying on a shared percentile cutoff.
icml-2026-adascale-adaptive-scaling-for-.tldr: AdaSCALE uses activation changes under small perturbations to adaptively separate familiar and out-of-distribution inputs.

paragraphs: Alterbute edits an object’s color, texture, material, or shape while preserving its perceived identity and surrounding scene. The challenge is deciding which visual properties may change without making the object seem like something else. Existing methods can either lose identity through insufficient supervision or impose constraints so tight that meaningful attribute changes become difficult.

The method combines flexible training with tighter control at inference. During training, a diffusion model receives an identity reference, a text description of desired attributes, and a background image with an object mask. It may change both the object’s intrinsic attributes and its external context. At inference, reusing the original background and mask restricts changes to the intended object attributes.

Supervision comes from Visual Named Entities: fine-grained categories such as a particular car model that preserve identifying features while permitting attribute variation. A vision-language model extracts these categories and attribute descriptions from a large public image dataset. The reported improvements over existing methods support this combination of flexible identity categories and explicit scene control for identity-preserving editing.
icml-2026-alterbute-editing-intrinsic-at.tldr: Alterbute combines flexible identity supervision with scene constraints to edit object attributes while preserving perceived identity.

paragraphs: Computers approximate functions such as the exponential using combinations of basic arithmetic operations. Traditional mathematical constructions often support arbitrarily high accuracy, but finite-precision arithmetic cannot retain unlimited digits. This paper asks whether designing directly for finite precision can uncover more efficient expressions than approaches built around the possibility of ever-increasing accuracy.

AutoNumerics-Zero uses evolutionary symbolic regression to search over programs made from basic operations. Starting with empty code, it constructs mathematical expressions without prior mathematical knowledge beyond those operations. This search can optimize objectives that are not differentiable, including operation count, allowing it to consider computational cost alongside approximation accuracy rather than requiring a fixed formula family.

The authors report programs that outperform established methods in this setting. Their highlighted result is a ten-operation exponential approximation reaching fourteen significant figures, with accuracy more than six orders of magnitude beyond previously known approximations of that size. The finding shows how an explicit finite-precision target can open opportunities for automated mathematical program discovery.
icml-2026-autonumerics-zero-automated-di.tldr: Evolutionary program search discovers efficient finite-precision function approximations, including a ten-operation exponential approximation accurate to fourteen significant figures.

paragraphs: Boltzmann Generators aim to sample molecular configurations at thermodynamic equilibrium efficiently. They combine a generative model with exact likelihoods and an importance-sampling correction. Most rely on normalizing flows, which introduce a tradeoff: discrete-time flows impose strict invertibility constraints, while continuous-time flows can make likelihood computation expensive.

This paper replaces the flow-based architecture with an autoregressive framework called ArBG. Generating configurations sequentially avoids the topological constraints associated with flows and allows interventions during the generation sequence. The approach also draws on architectures effective in large language models to improve scalability. Its contribution is a different modeling foundation for Boltzmann Generators, retaining the focus on efficient equilibrium sampling.

Experiments show improvements over flow-based models across all evaluated benchmarks, especially for larger peptides such as ten-residue Chignolin. The authors also introduce Robin, a transferable 132-million-parameter model trained with ArBG. On eight-residue systems, Robin reduces the reported zero-shot energy error by about 60% relative to the previous state of the art, demonstrating transfer benefits within the evaluated setting.
icml-2026-autoregressive-boltzmann-gener.tldr: Autoregressive Boltzmann Generators replace flow-based molecular sampling with sequential generation, improving benchmark performance and transfer to evaluated peptide systems.

paragraphs: Comparing two generated answers and aggregating preferences into rankings is a common way to evaluate models. A concern is that judges may prefer attractive writing or familiar styles over correct answers. This paper tests how closely such preference rankings agree with accuracy rankings in settings where ground-truth answers are available.

The authors convert five established benchmarks into free-form generation tasks and aggregate pairwise judgments using Elo. The resulting rankings have Spearman correlations above 0.9 with rankings based on correctness. Pairwise evaluation also substantially outperforms direct evaluation when the judge is weak. These results indicate that comparative judgments can recover useful accuracy ordering in the tested settings despite concerns about judge reliability.

Style and judge bias have only minor effects on the overall rankings, even though most comparisons involve answers that share the same correctness status. Within those pairs, repeating content after the final answer, termed echo, causally influences preference. Thus, a local stylistic bias can coexist with strong aggregate agreement between preference rankings and accuracy.
icml-2026-correct-looks-better-pairwise-.tldr: Across five benchmarks, pairwise preference rankings closely track accuracy rankings despite a detectable preference for repetition after final answers.

paragraphs: The paper examines markets where several strategic sellers price datasets for buyers with limited budgets. Each seller wants to maximize revenue, and an equilibrium would mean that no seller benefits from changing its price alone. Data complicates this problem because it is non-rivalrous: selling access does not consume the dataset as selling a physical item would.

The authors show that uniform pricing need not produce an exact Nash equilibrium. Their impossibility result also rules out a general guarantee of a 1.364-approximate equilibrium. They therefore allow more flexible, piecewise-linear convex pricing functions. With this flexibility, a pricing profile exists where no seller can double revenue by switching unilaterally to any uniform price.

That guarantee is specifically about deviations to uniform prices, which defines the scope of the approximate stability result. Simulations show fast convergence and empirical approximation guarantees better than the worst-case factor of two. Together, the theory and experiments suggest that richer pricing rules can restore useful stability in data markets where uniform pricing lacks general equilibrium guarantees.
icml-2026-equilibrium-pricing-in-oligopo.tldr: Flexible convex pricing can guarantee approximate stability against uniform-price deviations in data markets where uniform pricing need not admit equilibrium.

paragraphs: Role-play text-to-speech requires a voice to remain consistent with a character and scene across several conversational turns. Producing understandable speech alone does not satisfy this requirement. The paper addresses the difficulty of measuring speaking style objectively, which also makes it harder to train audio models to follow expressive role-play instructions.

The proposed metric, Mean Continuation Log-Probability, uses a pretrained large audio language model to assess stylistic continuity. It measures how likely ground-truth speech tokens are after a context containing the transcript, generated speech, and repeated transcript. This likelihood serves as a proxy for whether the generated speech supports a continuation in the desired style, drawing on the model’s in-context learning ability.

The authors also use the metric as a reinforcement learning reward and construct a large role-play speech dataset with scene and character annotations. Experiments show agreement with human judgments of stylistic consistency. Training with this reward improves both objective measures and subjective evaluations, supporting its use for evaluating and improving expressive speech.
icml-2026-evaluating-and-rewarding-lalms.tldr: MCLP uses speech continuation likelihood as a proxy for stylistic consistency and an effective training reward for role-play speech generation.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can predict waypoints for visual navigation, but guiding their outputs toward a task objective can move actions away from the patterns represented in training. Such drift can produce inefficient or unreliable trajectories. This paper proposes an inference-time method that pursues the task objective while avoiding large changes measured through Fisher geometry.

Fisher Preserving Guidance uses Outer Product Span Projection to constrain the update. A low-rank Jacobian factorization makes the computation require only one backward pass per step, enabling real-time use. Because the intervention operates during inference, it can guide an existing diffusion model without additional training. The method therefore addresses both the direction of guidance and its computational cost.

The authors also introduce Truncated Fisher Denoising Sensitivity as an uncertainty signal for blending multiple sampled actions robustly. Experiments cover Maze2D, PushT with existing Diffusion Policy weights, simulated visual navigation, and real robots. Consistent improvements over strong diffusion-policy baselines support combining constrained guidance with uncertainty-aware action blending in the evaluated control settings.
icml-2026-fisher-preserving-guidance-tra.tldr: Fisher-preserving guidance improves evaluated diffusion-control tasks by constraining inference updates and blending actions using an uncertainty signal.

paragraphs: Online reinforcement learning for flow-matching models commonly waits for an entire denoising trajectory before assigning a reward. This makes feedback expensive to obtain and ties individual actions to a score for the completed generation. The paper challenges the assumption that effective learning requires this full-trajectory evaluation.

Its method, iGRPO, replaces full rollouts with a single-step mapping that supplies an immediate reward at each denoising step. These rewards depend on the timestep, reflecting that the model behaves differently at different stages of generation. Evaluating actions locally provides more precise credit assignment and removes the need for multi-step stochastic differential equation rollouts to obtain the training feedback.

Across standard benchmarks, the authors report convergence 10.2 times faster than FlowGRPO alongside higher final alignment quality. This is evidence that reducing the delay and cost of reward computation can improve both efficiency and the learned result in the tested setting. The contribution centers on changing where feedback is assigned, making individual denoising decisions directly evaluable during online learning.
icml-2026-igrpo-fast-online-rl-for-flow-.tldr: iGRPO assigns timestep-dependent rewards to individual denoising actions, achieving faster convergence and better final alignment than FlowGRPO on evaluated benchmarks.

paragraphs: A language model can appear to have forgotten information when evaluated using greedy decoding, which selects the most likely continuation. This paper shows that information suppressed under that evaluation can reappear when outputs are sampled probabilistically. The distinction matters because successful suppression in one deterministic answer does not establish reliable forgetting across repeated sampled generations.

The authors introduce leak@k to measure the likelihood that supposedly forgotten knowledge resurfaces across k samples. Their systematic study uses TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP and finds persistent leakage across methods and tasks. The results indicate that current unlearning techniques often provide limited forgetting when evaluated under realistic sampling strategies, even when standard deterministic evaluations suggest success.

The paper also proposes RULE, an unlearning algorithm aimed at this evaluation criterion. It produces no observed information leakage over a large number of samples on TOFU and beats existing methods on MUSE for most tested sampling budgets. These findings support evaluating and training for repeated-sampling robustness; the TOFU result remains an empirical observation over the evaluated generations.
icml-2026-leak-k-unlearning-does-not-mak.tldr: Leak@k exposes information that resurfaces after unlearning under repeated probabilistic sampling, while RULE improves robustness on evaluated benchmarks.

paragraphs: Image watermarks are often added after generation by modifying pixels, which can introduce extra computation and visible artifacts. DistSeal moves watermark learning into the generative model’s latent space, the internal representation used before the final image is produced. The framework works across both diffusion and autoregressive image generators.

The approach first trains separate watermarking models on these latent representations. It then distills their behavior into either the image generator itself or the decoder that converts latent representations into images. This creates a route from a separately trained watermarking component to watermarking embedded within the generation process, reducing the need for an additional pixel-space operation.

The authors report competitive robustness and similar imperceptibility compared with pixel-space baselines, together with speedups reaching twentyfold. Their experiments also find that distilling latent watermarkers gives better results than distilling pixel-space watermarkers. The findings support latent space as a useful place both to learn image watermarks and to integrate them efficiently into generative models.
icml-2026-learning-to-watermark-in-the-l.tldr: DistSeal learns image watermarks in latent space and distills them into generators or decoders, delivering competitive robustness with up to twentyfold speedups.

paragraphs: The paper compares neural architectures by tracking how they change topological structure through their layers. It initially restricts every layer to a three-dimensional representation space. This isolates the effects of depth and activation from width, since adding dimensions can simplify structures that remain nontrivial in fewer dimensions. Three dimensions also make these transformations easier to visualize.

The analysis focuses on linking number, an invariant describing how loops link together. Measured by their ability to change linking numbers, residual connections and transformer attention have equal power. Both are strictly more powerful than feedforward networks with monotonic activations, which in turn exceed invertible and flow-based models. These comparisons concern the specified topological measure of expressivity.

Changing the activation can alter that hierarchy: nonmonotonic activations bring feedforward networks into the same expressivity class as ResNets and transformers. The authors support these claims with proofs and experiments and extend the results beyond three dimensions. The work suggests that topology can reveal architectural differences that help guide network design.
icml-2026-low-dimensional-topology-of-de.tldr: A topology-based analysis ranks neural architectures by their ability to change linking numbers and shows how nonmonotonic activations alter that hierarchy.

paragraphs: Labels produced by pretrained models can contain systematic errors tied to the structure of the inputs. This differs from treating label noise as random corruption. A single global error model can miss these local patterns, while estimating a separate noise-transition matrix for every example presents a tractability problem. MIND addresses the space between those extremes.

The framework decomposes a high-dimensional noise manifold into components associated with latent subspaces. Its Latent Decoupling Estimator dynamically assigns samples to structural clusters with consistent error patterns. This makes the noise structure identifiable without ground-truth anchor points. The key idea is to share an error model among structurally related examples rather than across the entire dataset or separately for every instance.

Evaluation progresses from controlled CIFAR-100 noise to S3DIS and ScanNet, where annotation errors connect directly to three-dimensional geometry. MIND significantly outperforms existing methods on these benchmarks and corrects zero-shot hallucinations from vision-language models such as OpenSeg. These results support its potential for transferring knowledge from foundation models while correcting their structured annotation errors.
icml-2026-mind-decoupling-model-induced-.tldr: MIND groups structurally related examples with shared error patterns to identify and correct systematic noise in model-generated labels.

paragraphs: Least privilege means giving a request only the access needed to accomplish its task. This paper brings that security principle inside language models by defining privilege as the internal computation reachable during a forward pass. Reducing privilege therefore reduces the set of functions the model can access, giving a concrete computational meaning to capability restriction.

The authors organize deployment control into three parts: a monitor gathers request-time signals, an allocator decides how much privilege to grant, and an enforcer applies that decision during inference. Their proposed Nested Least-Privilege Networks use a shape-preserving intervention indexed by rank. This supplies a smooth, reversible control mechanism for varying accessible computation without requiring separate models for each privilege level.

The reported results show privilege–utility tradeoffs that policies can use and selective suppression of targeted capabilities with limited collateral degradation across different policies. The broader contribution is a deployment framework in which requests receive different computational access. It demonstrates a way to control capability exposure internally while measuring how those restrictions affect useful behavior.
icml-2026-no-more-no-less-least-privileg.tldr: Least-privilege language models restrict reachable internal computation per request, enabling reversible capability control with measured utility tradeoffs.

paragraphs: Federated independence testing asks whether variables are statistically dependent using data distributed across clients. When clients have different data distributions, combining their evidence becomes difficult. The paper revisits existing methods and explains how this heterogeneity can undermine either the validity of their guarantees or their ability to detect dependence.

The proposed FedIT method combines copula-based marginal alignment with stacking-based aggregation. Alignment addresses differences in individual variable distributions, while aggregation emphasizes dependence within clients and reduces variation between clients. This division matters because a global test needs to retain the relationships present locally without letting client-to-client distribution shifts dominate the combined evidence.

The authors also accelerate aggregation and incorporate a privacy-preserving mechanism to make the approach more practical. They prove correctness and test validity, then evaluate performance on synthetic and real-world datasets. The experiments show superiority over existing methods in the studied settings. Together, the results connect a theoretically supported global test with an aggregation strategy designed specifically for heterogeneous clients.
icml-2026-powerful-and-theoretically-gua.tldr: FedIT aligns client distributions and aggregates within-client dependence to deliver a theoretically valid and empirically powerful federated independence test.

paragraphs: Rotary position encodings incorporate positional information into transformer attention by rotating token representations. This paper asks how that idea can apply to graphs, where relationships come from connectivity rather than a simple sequence of positions. The goal is to give attention access to graph structure through an encoding compatible with the rotary approach.

The proposed method, Wave-Induced Rotary Encodings, derives its rotations from the spectrum of the graph Laplacian. This ties token rotations to structural information about the graph. The authors show that WIRE recovers ordinary rotary position encoding on grids and depends on effective resistance, connecting the construction to a graph-based measure of connectivity.

Experiments report better performance on both synthetic and real-world graph learning tasks. WIRE is also compatible with linear attention, a property the abstract contrasts with bias-based relative position encodings. The contribution therefore combines a graph-aware rotation mechanism, theoretical links to established graph structure, and empirical gains without requiring the relative-position bias formulation.
icml-2026-rotary-position-encodings-for-.tldr: WIRE adapts rotary position encodings to graph structure using Laplacian-based rotations while remaining compatible with linear attention.

paragraphs: Event-camera classification often converts sensor events into frames or voxels before processing them. Those transformations can be expensive, require bulky models, and discard fine temporal detail. Representing events as point clouds offers another route, but existing approaches struggle to scale when spatial resolution increases or event sequences cover longer periods.

SECNet uses an Event Cloud representation and changes how events are organized and processed. Its Event-based Group and Sampling module incorporates event polarity into the network’s structure instead of treating polarity only as an input feature. This makes polarity part of the procedure that groups and selects events for subsequent feature extraction.

To handle growing event counts, SECNet extracts features in the frequency domain using the Fourier transform. The authors report that this substantially curbs the growth of multiply-accumulate operations while capturing spatial and temporal information. Experiments on ten event-based datasets support the network’s scalability, effectiveness, and efficiency. The approach addresses both the representation of event structure and the computational burden of processing larger event collections.
icml-2026-scalable-event-cloud-network-f.tldr: SECNet combines polarity-aware event grouping with Fourier-domain feature extraction to make event-cloud classification more scalable and efficient.

paragraphs: Unsupervised multi-source domain adaptation learns from several labeled source domains to perform well on an unlabeled target domain. A federated setting keeps raw data local, but adding many diverse sources can make existing adaptation methods computationally expensive or unstable. GALA is designed to address this scaling problem while retaining the federated setup.

Its alignment objective compares groups in a way that approximates pairwise alignment with linear complexity. GALA also uses a temperature-controlled weighting mechanism based on centroids to adjust which sources receive priority. Together, these components support stable, parallelizable training across heterogeneous sources, reducing the burden of alignment while allowing source contributions to change dynamically.

The authors introduce Digit-18, a benchmark combining eighteen datasets with synthetic and real-world domain shifts, to test high-diversity adaptation. Experiments report state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks and substantial improvements in larger settings where prior methods become computationally infeasible or fail to converge. The findings support group-wise alignment as a practical way to extend federated adaptation to more sources.
icml-2026-scaling-unsupervised-multi-sou.tldr: GALA scales federated domain adaptation through group-wise alignment and dynamic source weighting, improving results in high-diversity settings.

paragraphs: Estimating average treatment effects from streaming observational data requires handling new observations without retaining the entire history. The task becomes harder when treatment assignment and the process generating outcomes change over time. Offline balancing methods need full-data access, while parametric online models can become unreliable when their assumed form no longer fits.

The proposed method compresses the stream into feature coresets using discrepancy theory. These compact representations preserve covariate-balancing objectives over a rich nonparametric function class and support linear-time updates with bounded memory. The method then learns balancing weights directly, avoiding a parametric estimate of treatment-assignment probabilities. Balancing across an expressive function space also helps accommodate changes in outcome relationships.

The authors establish convergence guarantees with explicit memory and computation bounds. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show effectiveness and robustness, consistently outperforming the compared techniques. The contribution connects compact streaming storage with flexible balancing, making it possible to maintain the information needed for treatment-effect estimation while addressing shifts in both assignment and outcomes.
icml-2026-streaming-covariate-balancing-.tldr: Discrepancy-based feature coresets enable bounded-memory treatment-effect estimation with direct covariate balancing under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Constrained decoding forces a language model to follow an output format by removing invalid next-token choices. This ensures structural validity, but it can steer generation toward incorrect content when the model assigns little probability to valid continuations. The paper examines this tension between producing a valid structure and preserving the reasoning needed for a correct answer.

Draft-Conditioned Constrained Decoding separates those tasks into two inference stages. The model first generates an unconstrained draft, then produces a constrained answer conditioned on that draft. No additional training is required. The authors analyze this through a KL-projection perspective: draft conditioning increases probability assigned to feasible continuations and reduces the accumulated distortion caused by repeatedly enforcing constraints.

Across structured reasoning benchmarks, DCCD improves strict structured accuracy by up to approximately twenty-four percentage points. One reported case rises from 15.2% to 39.0% on GSM8K with a one-billion-parameter model. Smaller model pairs also match or exceed much larger constrained baselines, showing that a draft can improve parameter efficiency as well as structured-answer accuracy.
icml-2026-the-hidden-cost-of-structured-.tldr: Generating an unconstrained draft before constrained decoding improves structured-answer accuracy by reducing the distortion caused by format enforcement.

paragraphs: Sentence-level watermarking offers a way to mark generated text without requiring access to a model’s internal token-generation machinery. However, existing approaches can have low watermark success rates. This paper traces much of that problem to a mismatch between where sentence embeddings are likely to fall and the semantic regions accepted by the watermarking scheme.

X-Guard addresses this mismatch by optimizing both the embedding distribution and the partition of semantic space. It learns a more isotropic representation, making the embedding geometry less uneven across directions. Its A²PQ partitioning scheme aligns regions with centroids and approximately balances their probability mass. These changes aim to make successful watermark injection more likely.

Experiments across multiple models, languages, and attack settings show consistent improvements in robustness while preserving text fluency and practical deployability. The central contribution is a geometric explanation for injection failures and a method that responds to that explanation. It treats reliable watermarking as a joint problem of sentence representation and region design, rather than considering either component alone.
icml-2026-towards-reliable-marking-and-v.tldr: X-Guard improves sentence-level text watermarking by aligning embedding geometry with semantic regions used for watermark injection.

paragraphs: This paper studies regression across multiple groups that share an underlying structure but also have group-specific differences. Its key assumption is additive: each group’s function can be represented through shared structure plus a deviation. That setup creates an opportunity to borrow information across groups while retaining the features that make each group distinct.

The proposed procedure has two stages. First, it pools observations from all groups to estimate an overall mean function. Second, it learns an offset for each group and adds that offset to the pooled estimate. The authors establish upper bounds on squared-integrated estimation error for a broad class of nonparametric estimators under complexity and noise conditions.

For deep ReLU networks, they derive explicit convergence rates under hierarchical composition models, showing how the method can overcome the curse of dimensionality in that setting. They also examine conditions for faster rates through positive transfer, including simpler functions and pooling-based sample augmentation. Simulations and real-data experiments support the approach’s effectiveness alongside these conditional theoretical results.
icml-2026-transfer-learning-in-nonparame.tldr: A pooled regression estimate plus group-specific offsets enables transfer learning, with favorable error rates under shared additive structure and stated model conditions.

paragraphs: Generative reward models can explain their scores using task-specific evaluation principles. However, if they choose those principles after reading the response, the response can influence the standards used to judge it. The paper calls this Principle Drift: verbosity, self-praise, or invented justifications can shift criteria in ways that inflate rewards and reinforce reward hacking during training.

Independent Principle GRM separates criterion creation from evaluation. It first derives principles using only the question, then evaluates the answer using the question, response, and fixed principles. This keeps the criteria independent of the candidate’s content. A Principle Cache reuses principles within a group, maintaining consistent criteria while improving GRPO throughput by 23.66%.

In creative-writing training with Qwen3-8B, the authors report reduced reward hacking and improvements of up to 4.6 points on WritingBench and 7.1 points on CreativeWriting-v3. They also report state-of-the-art performance among open-source models. These findings support deciding what constitutes a good answer before inspecting the answer being rewarded.
icml-2026-unbiased-principles-robust-rew.tldr: IP-GRM generates evaluation principles before reading responses, reducing reward hacking and improving creative-writing training results.

paragraphs: Full-duplex voice agents listen and speak simultaneously, but evaluating conversational timing separately from task success leaves an incomplete picture. τ-Voice combines both: agents must complete verifiable tasks, follow domain policies, interact with an environment, and manage realistic spoken exchanges. Extending τ²-bench also allows direct comparisons between voice and text performance.

A controllable voice user simulator introduces varied accents, audio conditions, and turn-taking behavior. Simulation is decoupled from wall-clock time, allowing a capable language model to drive the simulated user without real-time constraints. Across 278 tasks, the benchmark measures first-attempt task completion alongside voice interaction quality, bringing practical conversation difficulties into the same evaluation as task execution.

GPT-5 with reasoning reaches 85% task completion, while voice agents achieve 31–51% in clean conditions and 26–38% with noise and diverse accents. The authors report retention of only 30–45% of text capability under realistic conditions. Qualitative analysis attributes 79–90% of failures to agent behavior, suggesting that the observed gap primarily reflects agent behavior within this evaluation setup.
icml-2026-voice-benchmarking-full-duplex.tldr: τ-Voice jointly evaluates task completion and realistic spoken interaction, revealing a substantial performance gap between tested voice agents and text capability.
